articleTitle: Arc furnace flicker assessment and prediction
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The paper gives the state of the art in arc furnace flicker assessment and prediction, taking account of the type of furnace (AC or DC), of the possible presence of compensating equipment (static VAr compensator, series reactor, synchronous condenser) and of the attenuation due to the transfer between HV and LV networks.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Progress in the long term testing of an all dielectric self supporting cable for power system use
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: All-dielectric, self-supporting, optical cables installed on power transmission lines with System voltages above 150 kV can suffer from sheath damage, caused by dry-band arcing induced by electrical coupling with the power circuits. There is a lack of data from actual installations on the duration, frequency and magnitudes of these low-current arcs. This information is necessary for the evaluation of accelerated testing regimes. The authors report the continuing results of a trial mounted in Scotland to monitor such events.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: 12 and 24 kV XLPE cables in Norway. Faults related to water treeing
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: In the end of 1990 approximately 13000 km three core XLPE cables were installed in the Norwegian 12 and 24 kV cable network. The fault rate of these cables has always been very low compared to other published results. Only 83 cables are reported to have failed in service. This corresponds to a fault rate for these cables as low as 0.1 faults/100 km three core cable in the year. 85% of the water treeing failures have occurred on the old construction with insulation screen made of semiconducting paint and tapes. However, five cables with an early type of strippable insulation screen have also failed due to long vented water trees from this screen after 10 years of service. Only limited lengths of this cable are installed in the Norwegian network. In spite of this favourable fault statistics the Norwegian cable construction has been changed several times. One of the purposes for these changes has been to further improve the cable with respect to water ingress and subsequently the risk of water tree initiation and growth.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A simulation model for transformer internal faults base for the study of protection and monitoring systems
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The study of internal faults in transformers, i.e. the calculation of the fault current and its external detection (phase currents) as a function of the location and the amplitude of the fault, is of great interest. This situation has led the authors to manufacture a special, multiple output transformer. This device, designed on the basis of a 100 kVA MV/LV transformer, has enabled them to carry out numerous turn-to-turn and turn-to-earth short-circuits. In association with these tests, they have developed a digital model of the transformer, validated by the actual measurements. This model, when applied to a HV network transformer, enables the efficiency of the usual protection devices to be examined, in particular that of the transformer differential protection.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Estimation of annual coincident peak demand and load curves based on statistical analysis and typical load data
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The estimation of annual coincident peak demand has traditionally been performed by different empirical methods. Research shows that if the customer loads are normally distributed the total load can be computed by a method using statistical analysis and typical load cues for each class of customer. In order to use this method the different customers must be classified and typical load profiles must be measured for each of them. A method which combines typical load curves and statistical methods is described. The authors show how this method generates other important parameters which even small utilities need in network planning and for other purposes related to the situation in Norway with the new Energy Act that will promote free market trade and a common carrier principle. The method can be used both to calculate total peak demand in a total network, and for special calculations for each customer group. The users of the method will benefit when making network calculations, in power demand forecasting, tariff calculations, general least cost utility planning, and for demand side management studies.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Validation tests and applications of a model for demand-side management studies in residential load areas
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The aim of the paper is to illustrate a computer program which permits to simulate both single family and large-area daily load profiles, starting from the electric energy end uses. The paper describes also the method adopted and the results of the comparison between the model simulations and some load recordings. Finally the application of a set of load control policies is simulated by means of the described model. As regards the assessment of the most effective control policy, new methods are illustrated to perform a more adequate economic and financial evaluation of the above mentioned measures.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Single-phase faults on compensated neutral medium voltage networks
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The authors reiterate the reasons that justified a two-stage evolution of the neutral earthing of the French medium voltage networks. In the context of overall coherence, EDF are aiming to guarantee: coordination of insulation for our MV and LV networks and for LV customers; safety of people and equipment (taking into account touch voltage, step voltage, coupling phenomena); a better quality of supply; and conformity of their practices to standards. Network experiments carried out over the last four years have confirmed their theories and validated expected solutions. Specifications for new devices have been established, based on functional requirements of the distributor.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The application of disturbance recorders for cost effective protection and switchgear monitoring and maintenance
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The operation and performance of circuit breakers and protection equipment is being monitored by microprocessor based disturbance recorders that are linked to the electricity utility's SCADA system. The recorders are able to record protection operating times, the circuit breaker mechanism response times, and the currents interrupted by the circuit breaker under fault conditions. The values of fault current interrupted can be accumulated for each circuit breaker and be used to optimise the post fault maintenance regime. A databank of the information is being assembled to allow condition based maintenance to be introduced for circuit breakers and protection equipment.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Peak shaving with batteries
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: Recently electric utilities have paid increased interest to load management with batteries. The authors study the possibilities of batteries to perform peak shaving at the customer side of the kWh-meter. The economic efficiency is discussed as a function of tarification formula and the time duration of the peak to be shaved. Battery and power electronics technologies involved are presented and commented upon. The service expected from the batteries is more severe than in common applications. Therefore, battery tests have been carried out at Laborelec and results after a one half year test program are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Expert systems to support network switching
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The techniques for the control of electrical power distribution networks are changing rapidly with the use of manual and paper based systems being replaced by computer aided techniques. The authors report work on two expert systems that are designed to support these developments. The Switching Schedule Production Assistant (SSPA)-designed to assist with the writing and management of switching schedules and which supports the control engineer in checking and authorising the schedule steps as they are carried out; and a Switching Checking Module (SCM) based on the rule checking part of SSPA for incorporation into a control room graphics system to provide real time checking of proposed switching actions and to warn of any potential problems immediately prior to carrying out the switching. The authors describe the technical aspects of the development of the two systems and also describe their role in the changing climate of operational practice and techniques for network control.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new overhead line concept based on covered conductors
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: A new overhead line concept based on covered conductors is introduced in the 24 kV distribution system. However, a neutral evaluation is necessary to clarify the service reliability in the Norwegian exposed climate. After one year in service in a coastal area the corrosion attack caused by simulated insulation damages is surprisingly high and can not be neglected. Further investigations must be carried out to clarify the factors which influence the simulation of lightning before recommendations for arcing and overvoltage protection can be given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design of a measurement program to characterize distribution system power quality
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The authors describe the design of a sampling and measurement program (sponsored by the Electric Power Research Institute, RP3098-1) to characterize distribution power supply quality in the United States. The program involves placing 300 monitors on sites in 25 utilities over a 2 year period. Power quality is measured in terms of frequency, magnitude and other characteristics of deviation from continuous supply of sinusoidal waveform power.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Fault location using fault distance measurement of digital relays
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: For a radial distribution network a method is presented for the distance metering of digital relays. The experiences in operation are very satisfactory. In combination with short circuit indicators a considerable reduction can be achieved in locating faults in the distribution system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Harmonics in MV and LV distribution systems: present and future levels
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: Slow but progressive changes in the nature of loads connected to the electric system have been witnessed for some years. Moreover, the large scale dissemination of these new disturbing loads may increase the 'background noise' level of the system and increases the risk of producing harmonic disturbances in all points of the system, especially at the connection points of reactive power compensation capacitors. In a first stage, the paper proposes an analysis of harmonic disturbances in distribution and transmission systems from sample readings made in MV/LV and HV/MV substations representing French Substations at large. The second part of the study consists of identifying these disturbing sources at different levels: domestic customer; MV/LV substation; and HV/MV substation. A statistical computation model of harmonic disturbances is then created from measurement results. It is used to identify the level of harmonics in any system with the knowledge of the number of domestic customers fed by this system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Planning the islanding scheme of a regional power producer
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: A power system can be divided into islands in the case of serious system disturbances. The authors discuss the types of power system disturbances, methods available for system protection and especially strategies for controlling the underfrequency islanding and island operation. Dynamic simulation studies were made concerning three Finnish municipal energy utilities owning local power generation. The results are presented as general principles which aid any power producer in planning its islanding scheme. These include methods for selecting the island area and suitable load shedding and reactive power compensation practices for this area. In addition, the earth-fault relay coordination during the island operation is discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A cooperative approach towards the solution of complex decision problems in energy management and electricity networks
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The authors present the experience of Iberdrola (Spain) and EA Technology (UK) in the development and use of expert systems applied to the control/supervision of electricity networks. The need to expand the scope of their existing stand-alone expert systems by integrating new information and new capabilities has moved these two companies to enter the emerging area of distributed artificial intelligence (DAI), joining forces in the ESPRIT project ARCHON, the objective of which is to produce a general framework for cooperating expert systems. The main objectives of the Iberdrola application are disturbance detection, identification of permanent faults, evaluation of network status, preparation of a restoration plan and tracking of network evolution. The EA Technology application integrates fault diagnosis both at high and low voltage, security analysis, generation of safe switching schedules, lightning detection and collates information between these individual systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An intelligent user interface for emergency operation
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The screen displays at the individual control room workplaces are the crucial constituent for man-machine communication efficacy in modern-day network control systems. Today, the first systems with full-graphics displays are already in operation. The authors describe the most useful graphics screen display technology and user interface features. The authors describe these features and their use in network operation and control.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Conduit inspection robot and small conduit after-laying method
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The construction of a new optical fiber cable communication system involves the costly operation of installing the cables underground, and, in addition, such installation work is subject to numerous regulations. It is therefore preferable, to incorporate new optical fiber cables within existing conduit, into which power cable has already been installed. However, if any collapse or blockage has occurred within the existing power cable conduit, this may make the inclusion of optical fiber cables impracticable. Therefore, it is necessary to have a device which is capable of inspecting the condition inside of the existing power cable conduit, prior to the optical fiber cables being installed. Tokyo Electric Power Company and Fujikura Ltd. have jointly developed the self-advancing conduit inspection robot, and the 'small conduit after-laying method' for including a small conduit for optical fiber cables, within an existing power cable conduit. The authors describe the robot and experience with it in practice.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Strategy for upgrading the transformer substations taking into account the structure of the medium-voltage network
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The authors using the example of transformer substations, how the total amount of necessary upgrading expenditure for selected equipment can be quantified. The initial situation is analyzed by means of a representative random sample. Taking into account further influential factors, a hierarchy for clearing the enormous amount of work to be done can be deduced from the upgrading strategy. The results obtained allow factors to be determined which are of importance in the context of upgrading expenditure. Extension and modification of the medium-voltage network to form open-operation ring systems allow primarily the use of three-panel gas-insulated medium-voltage switchgear in both renovation and reconstruction of transformer substations. Selected fault-susceptible equipment, such as the solid-insulation high-voltage distribution boards, will be replaced. With the results obtained, the procedure is a useful tool for the preparation of business-strategic decisions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Advanced monitoring technologies for the evaluation of demand-side management programs
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The aim of this paper is to provide an assessment of the state-of-art of the technologies that can be used for monitoring demand side management programs. This paper examines the following techniques that can be used for end use monitoring: field test equipment, general purpose data loggers; run-time data loggers; utility-oriented data loggers; energy management systems; smart meters; nonintrusive load monitoring; and building automation. Additionally, the paper points out research and development activities whose implementation can contribute to the more accurate and cost-effective evaluation of the performance of end use technologies.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new software tool for economical optimisation of low voltage networks
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The author describes a software tool giving support when planning the most economical low voltage distribution network. An easy-to-use software tool has been developed in order to simplify the design of the low voltage network. Based on certain pre-conditions like cost of cables, type of cables to be used, maximum voltage drop and cost of losses, the program calculates the right cables to obtain the most economical network, i.e. the total cost of construction and losses is minimised. Further, the program can test the network on several safety requirements (like contact voltage) and it enables the user to modify the network in order to meet these requirements. As the program is to be used by people who are not familiar with computers, attention is payed to user-friendliness. The program is menu driven and can be run by using only a few keys or a mouse, which reduces the risk of making errors and makes the program user-friendly.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Live working diagnosis of joints of overhead lines
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: An assessment of all the surveys of joints for fifteen years indicates that they constitute a weak point in overhead lines. Internal corrosion or a defective realisation is the original cause, which leads, later on, to the increase of the contact resistance and therefore of the temperature of the joint. The authors examine how the joints are made and what phenomena occur in their ageing. This analysis leads to retention of the most influential factors and a proposal for modelling of the joint and of the evolution of its degradation in the past. The authors then describe the ageing prediction capacities made by a model in several selected situations, because they appear in operation. These simulations make it possible to extract the strong tendencies and from them conclusions about the service life of joints. They have repercussions on initial quality and in situ controls of the joints and maintenance of overhead lines. Finally, the authors examine a method of live working measurement of the electric resistance of joints.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new approach to arcing fault detection on overhead distribution feeders
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The use of nonpower frequency components for power system relaying has been known for more than fifty years, however, the use of high frequency components on relaying has not been seriously looked at. This paper seeks to remedy this situation. This paper investigates a novel technique for fault detection and location on overhead distribution networks based upon detecting fault induced high frequency components introduced on the line.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Voltage and current conditioner for distribution networks reconfigurable to UPS
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: A very great effort has been done during the last decade on spreading the application of static power converters to power distribution lines. This paper shows work on new distribution line conditioners based on high frequency commutated active filtering. This work has been developed in the scope of a PIE project leadered by Iberdrola S.A. whose aim is the development of 25 kVA to 1000 kVA conditioners for low voltage three phase standard distribution lines. The objective of the project is to find power topologies with better performances than those of the classical conditioners, but with a lower cost than in the case of uninterruptible power supplies. A reconfigurable power topology has been chosen which normally works as a series voltage conditioner and a parallel current conditioner linked by a common DC bus. In case of a line outage, the current conditioner acts an an inverter which is able to feed 30% of the nominal load during 200 ms. It is considered that this short storage time can eliminate more than 90% of the line outages.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Amorphous metal transformer cores save energy and capacity investment
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: Studies of distribution systems in the United States indicate that approximately 60% of distribution system losses are attributed to distribution transformers, with core losses accounting for 80% of the transformer loss, or about 45% of total system losses. The authors describe transformer core development that led to commercially available amorphous metal transformers and the analysis of the economic benefits to utility systems if strategies regarding the use of amorphous metal transformers for efficiency improvements, energy conservation, or demand side management are implemented. They also discuss the environmental concerns over power plant emissions, and establish the contribution amorphous transformers can make to reduced emissions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: EDF network automation policy
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: EDF has announced a minimal quality objective for 1995. The technical policy applied to reach this objective rests upon actions taken on the structure, network reliability and automation. The gradual establishment of remote controlled switches during this period of time will enable the acquisition of a well grounded operation feedback resulting in the improvement of equipment specifications and in actions aimed to make the network more reliable. The quality objectives beyond 1995, which are currently being defined, will take into account the customers' sensitivity.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The role of SMS (substation monitoring systems) in enhancing protection and control functions
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The basis of modern, microprocessor-based station control is an information bus, connecting all feeder units together. The SMS (substation monitoring system) is a part of the SCS (substation control system). The SMS deals mainly with the analog measuring quantities, the signals and the settings of the measuring, protection and regulation functions. Basically, all feeder-orientated tasks are performed in feeder units, where all feeder-related data are also stored. These feeder units are linked by the mentioned (serial) information bus, allowing the free exchange of information between all feeder units and the hierarchical higher levels, like substation units, network etc. The functionality is given by the software and I/O circuits only and comprises protection, measurement, regulation etc. The protection functions are autonomous. Based on this concept-called 'PYRAMID'-a lot of substations have been designed and equipped.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: LV network planning tools at EDF
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: A management system for the low voltage networks must enable the customer to be informed and the planner's objectives to be met. With regard to the planner, the maximal voltage drop on the LV networks and the compliance with the admissible load flow in the structures are the major two requirements to be complied with. At Electricite de France, a computerised system has been developed. It consists of: a technical database (GDO-BT) which contains the physical characteristics of the networks and, for each customer, information issued from the billing files; a statistical computation model (BAGHEERA) to evaluate the electrical variables of the service quality; and the design software programs (CRIT-BT, INVEST-BT, PANTER-BT) enabling the management and planning of LV networks. To complement this statistical approach of the network planning, it may be necessary in some specific cases to make measurements in MV/LV substation. The TILT software program enabling the processing of measured data is presented. Its completion is currently in progress.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Sag increases resulting from conductor creep on medium-voltage transmission lines, and the problem of measuring sag on live overhead lines
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: From experiences and laboratory tests it can be seen that the sag increases considerably during the operational period of overhead transmission lines. Because of lack of knowledge of this fact, the changes of sag is not always taken into calculation in the phase of planning. The authors show how the results of long-time creep strain measurement in the laboratory can be used in planning of overhead transmission lines. An example illustrates how the alteration in sag caused by conductor creep is dependent on the span length. The increases in sag are extrapolated for an operational period of 30 years. The example shows that for a medium voltage overhead transmission line in a 200 m span the sag after 30 years can increase up to 70 cm. The sag control of existing overhead lines is possible only when an adequate knowledge of the conductor temperatures is available. On disconnected lines, the air temperature at conductor height requires to be taken into account. The authors show possible ways of measuring the temperatures of conductors on live transmission lines.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Substation grounding grid design with the aid of a computer program
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The paper covers design considerations of AC substation grounding grids and describes a computer program that was developed to assist in the design of such grids. The program provides a scientific, technically acceptable and economically viable solution to substation grounding grid designs based on IEEE Std 80. The program is user friendly, requiring only basic engineering and computer knowledge.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Temperature monitoring of XLPE-insulated power cables by means of optical fibres
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The authors report on the design principle involved in integrating optical fibres in the copper wire screens of XLPE-insulated power cables and on the tests carried out. Contrary to the usual application, the transmission of information, the authors point out the sensory properties of optical fibres. These allow the temperature of the power cable to be determined, e.g. the influence of additional power cables and other heat sources (hot spots), on the permissible cable load, can be considered. The measuring principle, its accuracy and limits are described. The tests were first of all carried out on medium voltage cable. Because the cable voltage does not materially affect the results of the tests, the pilot installation, in 110 kV XLPE-insulated cable in commercial operation, is presented. The first results of the measurements are shown and analysed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A coordinated earthing system design methodology for substations
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The traditional approaches to earthing system design are proving inadequate due to increased constraints, including: increases in system capacity and complexity, the use of microprocessor based equipment in substations, increased interaction with industrial installations (e.g. mines, pipelines and telecommunications networks), reduced substation areas, professional liability and tighter financial constraints. A guide presenting design principles and guidelines, as well as implementation and testing methodologies for earthing systems in Australian conditions, is in the final stages of preparation. The authors provide a description of the integrated design package, introduces a coordinated design methodology, and the technical background to the computational techniques and design methods used in the guide and associated software.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Application and evaluation of a new concept for compact series compensation for distribution networks
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: A newly developed distribution series power capacitor concept has been field tested in a joint project between Gullspangs Kraft AB and ABB Power Systems AB. Due to growing load, a voltage profile problem was experienced in a 12 kV radial distribution system in a rural area. Series compensation was found to be a suitable and cost efficient way to improve the voltage and the loadability of the system. The series capacitor has performed successfully in service since commissioning in November 1990. The paper describes the actual network and the evaluation of different possibilities to improve the voltage and the loadability of the system. Estimation of differences in investment costs are shown. It further gives a description of the series capacitor equipment and its basic performance. The paper finally reports on general experience gained during the field test period, especially with regard to the particular line fault statistics.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Study of the life consumption of distribution transformers and assessment of end-of-life criteria
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: It is generally accepted that the reliability of power transformers decreases with the ageing of their insulation system. This ageing is due mainly to the thermal degradation of the mechanical characteristics of the insulating materials. Therefore, the Municipal Energy Board of Turin decided to assess the thermal ageing of the whole population of their 6 kV transformers and to base the criteria for transformer selection on the degree of ageing reached by the single units. The authors present the study made for the above purpose. The approach used was both theoretical (loss of life calculations) and experimental temperature rise tests, dielectric tests and short-circuit tests.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Monitoring of primary circuit temperatures and breaker condition in a substation
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: Different temperature-related fail-mechanisms in switchgear are discussed. A new high potential temperature monitoring system is presented. The new system can give early warnings of beginning fail-mechanisms, and can also be used to allow intentional short-period overloading. Relevant alarm criteria are analysed. Field tests where temperature data were sent on telephone lines are described. Different parameters, relevant for monitoring of circuit breaker condition are discussed. Improved versions of the condition monitor for the HPA-breaker, presented in a CIRED-report 1985, are presented. The possibility to integrate temperature monitoring, breaker monitoring and other monitoring units into a flexible data communication system is discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Optimization of the design of future HV/MV EDF substations using dependability studies and value analysis: the example of a medium voltage switchboard
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: Improving the quality of electric power supplies while controlling costs is the ambitious objective of Electricite de France. To achieve this, a focus on reliability in infrastructure and equipment from the specification stage onwards by EDF and in the manufacturing stage is a precondition. The authors present the new approach adopted by EDF for specifying future equipment in HV/MV substations by the user and manufacturers. This approach is based on methods already employed in other industrial fields, namely value analysis and dependability assessment, methods which require adaptation to the specific features of the MV switchgear.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: CUSTOM POWER: an opportunity for energy conservation
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The CUSTOM POWER concept, initiated by EPRI, provides the electric utility industry with a low loss technology, in the range of 0.5% to 1% to meet the power supply quality needs of customers who have sophisticated, sensitive loads. In addition to receiving quality power, customers can avoid the significant investment and electrical losses that are the result of customer installed power conditioning equipment. Judging from the current growth rate, a preliminary study indicates that CUSTOM POWER technology can offer energy savings up to 20000 MW by the year 2015. The authors discuss details of the development work in various power electronics controllers and raises the issue of economics for further discussion.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The introduction and utilization of a modern, technical information system at Scandinavian utilities
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: Experience from Scandinavian utilities which have been successful in introducing network information systems, show that success depends on establishing a project plan for the introduction. This project should be controlled by the utilities' management, and must define responsibilities, economic and personnel resources. The introduction plan should deal with the following elements: evaluating different network information systems; installing the system; establishing the system in the utility organization; and operation of the system. The authors describe the NETBAS technical information system designed to cover the requirements of power supply utilities considering network expansion and operation planning, maintenance management and system documentation. At the same time it also meets user demands regarding man machine interface, low price, modern technology and a smooth integration into the utilities' organization.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Planning and quality policies at Electricite de France
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The authors discuss the power quality policies and network planning up to 1985. A new policy was implemented in 1986 which extends to 1995. There will then be a further review of policies in 1995. The author discusses the new MV supply contract and medium and short term planning with respect to the objectives set out by these policies.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Optical crystal based current measurement device using the Faraday effect
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The authors describe how an optical crystal based current sensor has been successfully demonstrated and classified to the 5P10 protection C.T standard of BS 3938. Problems concerning vibration and temperature effects have been addressed. Magneto-optic crystal based devices are assessed and their performance compared.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: LAURE: an operational expert system for the analysis of faults occurring on medium voltage networks
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: To better meet the expectations and requirements of its customers, EDF has been making every effort to improve the quality of the electrical energy supplied. Ensuring the reliability of medium voltage units is a key part of this strategy. The increased levels of reliability come as the result of new methods and tools for the diagnostics, upkeep and renewal of MV overhead networks. In this respect, EDF has developed a method termed 'auscultation' which consists of analysing all the electrical incidents affecting a medium-voltage feeder and identifying the sources of transient faults. To generalize this method and improve its efficiency, the EDF R&D department has drawn up the specifications and modelled a tool for auscultation aid. The mock-up, produced using an expert system approach, enabled requirements to be clearly defined and suggested a number of possible solutions using current technology. The functions of the LAURE software product are described in detail, together with the initial operating results.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Determination of the supply quality for specific consumers and ways to improve this supply quality
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The authors suggest that if a power supply company wish to aim at a certain supply quality it must also be able to check whether or not the quality standard is upheld. The supply quality for a specific consumer, however, cannot be determined by means of statistics alone but calls for supplementary calculations based on the components and topology of the network. The authors describe a method of calculation of interruption frequency and duration, especially with a view to the interruption time used for the localization of faults in the MV network. Further, the results of an investigation are described in which the method was used for a comparison of the supply reliability for ring networks, feeder networks, and satellite networks. The description comprises the improvements of the supply quality which can be obtained by the use of short-circuit indicators, remote control switches, and emergency generators.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Co-generation power plants in MV and LV networks
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: A cogeneration power plant simultaneously converts fossil energy into heat and electricity. Its efficiency is comparable to that of a boiler. However, its conversion is more economical, since part of the output energy represents high-valued electricity. The author details how he has developed a novel concept in order to optimize the use of fossil energy while minimizing the emission of pollutants. The cogeneration power plant is equipped with a heat buffer. During the daily electrical load peak it is electrically, else thermally controlled. Thus, energy storage and transport are performed in the physically most adequate form, viz. in the heat buffer and in the electrical power system respectively. The power system transports the energy to two types of consumers whose peak loads appear at different times of the day: first to thermal consumers with electrical heat pumps equipped with a short term buffer which make use of the environmental heat; and second to electrical consumers for whom it acts as peak power plant. The stability criterion for connecting a plant to the power system is derived.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An automatic meter-reading system (AMRS) by mobile radio
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: So far in China tens of millions of kWh meters have been read manually. Utilities are looking for alternatives to labour-intensive manual meter reading for a long time. The automatic meter-reading system (AMRS) by mobile radio is a new method of automatic measurement and a new way of management which fits to Chinese conditions. The authors describe the principle idea, composition, characteristic, function, cost, and testing results of AMRS and discuss some technical problems encountered.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Customer communications in system emergencies using voice processors
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: At Midlands Electricity PLC, performance is measured against certain standards of service; one of these standards refers to telephone answering. During December 1990 the United Kingdom suffered a particularly severe snow storm that caused widespread disruption of electricity supplies. An analysis of telephone answering performance during this emergency showed that improvements were required. The authors discuss the use of voice processors for telephone answering during electrical system emergencies and during office hours. The advantages of using this system are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Field bus: an appropriate solution to satisfy operational requirements and to have open digital control systems
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: EDF decided to develop a new technical stage for the control and the protection of HV/MV substations. It will be put into operation by 1995. It will be digital and organized around an 'open' field bus. Such an architecture is technically and economically feasible, as the installation achieved by CEE around FIP field bus on a large industrial site shows.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A fully programmable multi function meter (for power systems)
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The Ferraris electricity metering technology has proved to be long lasting reliable and cost effective for most applications. In complex industrial metering where multi tariff facilities are required the Ferraris technology is less flexible and more costly. A fully programmable multifunction meter (designated PPM) is described which fully satisfies all measurement criteria and provides for programmable tariffs. The interface with remote communications facilities and the rest of the integrated meter system has been described. With such a system, load profile data may be obtained enabling users to optimise demand and choice of tariff.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Modal noise in optical fibre transmission systems
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The authors present the results they have obtained on several optical links degraded by modal noise. They are analyzed to show that modal noise can cause a serious problem in optical transmission by producing an important degradation of the bit-error-rate. The authors show that the measurement of the bit-error-rate in optical links is a difficult task because modal noise tends to group errors in packets. Finally, they present an attractive aspect of modal noise for estimating the mechanical vibrations of aerial optical cables.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Effects of multiple stroke lightning impulse currents on ZnO arresters
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: Multiple stroke lightning ground flashes can impose surges of exceptional severity on the arresters used to protect exposed distribution system equipment. The authors report laboratory studies of the effects of representative multiple impulse currents on zinc-oxide surge arresters of distribution type. The results indicate that sextuple 8/20 mu s currents can cause damage to arresters not evident with standard lightning current tests.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Changing the structure of existing networks with regard to the voltage levels and network configuration
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The TIWAG (Tiroler Wasserkraftwerke AG) with its rural structure of supply operates two medium voltage levels with nominal voltages of 10 kV and 25 kV. There were two possibilities for selection: 20 kV or 30 kV. Considerations of the technical/economical arguments showed that 30 kV would be the better solution for the future. The measures which prepare the reconstruction process were fixed and considerations about the reconstruction process were made. The technical and commercial backgrounds and decisive factors for the choice of the medium voltage level of 30 kV and for the adjustment of both the medium voltage levels of 10 kV and 25 kV, which were in competition, are described. Additionally, the assigned time scale for changing the operating-voltage from 25 kV to 30 kV and from 10 kV to 25 (30) kV are also described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Optimal allocation of distribution investment
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: Management and owners of electricity supply authorities are regularly confronted by decisions for the allocation of limited capital and operating funds between dissimilar project types. The author presents a method for the prioritization of a wide range of dissimilar electricity industry spending proposals, some of which target improvements to the total supply system, while others target improvements to only a small geographic area. The method is based on an evaluation of the various components of the benefit of each project, compared with the project cost.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: User experience with a modern telemetering system (for power networks)
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: In 1989, VEW-Vereinigte Elektrizitatswerke Westfalen AG-employed a modern, future-oriented telemetering system of type DATAGYR20, provided by Messrs Landis & Gyr for determining the load curves on the 110 kV networks of its four regional management divisions, to provide in-plant measurement in connection with internal billing transactions. The telemetering system comprises four central computers together with transmitting meters and encoders, which are installed at appropriate measuring points. The metering values are transmitted to the central computer via a VEW owned communication network. Here the authors describe how after a 2 year operating period, the system has proved an outstanding success in terms of reliability, including transmission reliability, and the recording of results in report and graph form.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The development of aerodynamic vibration-proof insulated wire for overhead distribution lines
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The authors conducted static and dynamic wind tunnel tests to simulate aerodynamic vibration on a snow-accretionless insulated wire. They also constructed a field wire testing system to observe vibrations on the wire with a Vibrec recorder and video tape recording. The authors describe the results of these tests, and also the results obtained so far in developing of low-lift snow-accretionless insulated wire that can restrain aerodynamic vibration.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Ground wire with integrated optical fibres on a 40 year-old high-voltage overhead line provides new data transmission paths for the Austrian Federal Railways
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: In 1989, the Austrian Federal Railways (OBB) started to retrofit an existing 110 kV overhead line and to provide it with a ground wire with integrated optical fibers. However, part of the line sections are up to 40 years old, i.e. a number of specific design constraints had to be borne in mind when implementing the project. A ground wire with integrated optical fibers has been designed so as to be able to replace the existing conventional ground wire without requiring any major changes in pole statics. The authors describe the tests conducted on the fiber optical ground wire, the laying and installation method, and provides an outlook for the expected use of such a wire.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Service experience with numerical relays in distribution systems
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The utility Energieversorgung Oberfranken operates its 20 kV distribution systems in predominantly rural areas with Peterson Coil earthed neutrals and in urban areas with a high percentage of power cables solidly grounded. The individual load areas are fed by some 60, 110/20 kV substations, initially each with only one 40 MVA power transformer, which will not be duplicated until system growth demands it. Therefore, for system availability, in case of loss of one system component, the 110 kV system, as well as the 20 kV distribution system, is meshed. This system configuration requires fast and selective fault clearance, as well as efficient communication facilities for system restoration. Furthermore, for enhancement of system security, comprehensive fault reporting was required for preventive maintenance. It is the utility's policy to minimize the total costs of the distribution systems i.e. initial equipment costs, as well as operation and maintenance over their entire life time. These considerations lead to a fully numerical relay and control concept.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Canadian national power quality survey
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: An increasing number of polluting electrical and electronic loads are being connected to today's electrical distribution systems. With this comes the potential for increased customer complaints about 'alleged' power supply quality problems affecting the performance of 'sensitive' electronic equipment. The Canadian Electrical Association (CEA) is taking a proactive approach to this problem and has started a two year survey of power quality across Canada. The authors present a detailed discussion of what data is being captured for this survey, new techniques being used to analyze the data, and how the results are being displayed to show a comprehensive, high-level summary of the power quality measured at each sample site. The authors also discuss the technical requirements for the power line monitors that were chosen, and the rationale behind the monitor thresholds being used for this survey. A sample survey site report is also shown and discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Open and distributed information systems for distribution, fiction or reality?
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: As Spain's leading Electric Power Utility and the third largest in Europe, Iberdrola serves a market whose customers are spread over an area of 190000 sq. kms. The Company's integration plan relies basically on the business project, and as a tool, uses an information system plan which unifies criteria, ensures coherence in procedures and operations, and optimizes the supply quality for the customer. The authors describe the Distribution Facilities and Resources Integrated Information System (SIGRID), and its distributed development on open and standardized platforms, whose pilot test is to be implemented in the first half of 1993.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Computer-aided distribution network maintenance, rehabilitation and replacement planning
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The authors describe computer-based tools under development in Norway for MV/LV distribution network maintenance, rehabilitation and replacement planning. An overview is given of both the overall planning system and the corresponding system modules and tools. The authors focus on two different kinds of inspection data acquisition tools and a network information system, NETBAS with application modules for network analyses and maintenance management. One data acquisition system covers overhead lines and MV/LV substations, while the other covers street lighting. Both systems utilize hand-held computers.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: SUBSTATION EQUIPMENT
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED

articleTitle: Planner support in selecting investments in the power distribution network
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The authors give an account of planner support in selecting investments in the power distribution network. A prototype system for selecting investments has been produced for a microcomputer. The main software functions and environment are presented. The prototype was devised for the technical and economic planning of the investments to be made in the next planning period. Knowledge techniques were used for prioritising investments. The next stage will be the development of a project creating links with the corporate planning of the electric utility and the resulting network development goals.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Technical communication between customers and electric utilities in Sweden
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: On the Swedish electricity market, Vattenfall AB is responsible for about 50% for the electrical energy generated, and the remaining 50% are supplied by private and municipal utilities. Around 300 municipally (62%), privately (27%) and state (11%) owned utilities are responsible for the task of power distribution. Due to price increases and taxation, the price of electricity has increased in recent years from a low level to an appreciably higher level. The authors argue that because of the higher price of electricity, it is economically advantageous to use technical communication with customers, in order to restrict the energy and power demand both of customers and of distribution and generation utilities. Moreover, deregulation on the Swedish electricity market will increase the value of technical communication with customers.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Increasing power supply reliability in a large chemical plant taking system dynamics into account
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The dynamic behaviour of in-plant generators and of induction motor loads is compared before and after extension of the power system based on the example of a large chemical plant. The stability behaviour of the generators and motors with respect to active power and reactive power is taken into consideration in dimensioning the decoupling criteria for splitting the power system into isolated power subsystems when severe power system faults occur. The active and reactive power dynamic characteristics prior to and subsequent to decoupling are primarily responsible for the decoupling criteria and the tripping times for the tie circuit breakers. The dynamic behaviour of the plant on power system faults is tested by means of simulation. Effectiveness of the selected measures can thus be depicted and compared. Changes in dynamic behaviour subsequent to extension of the power system are taken into account in the design of the power system and of the protection measures.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Halogen free MV polymeric cable for power distribution
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The increased use of ZH cables has forced the evolution of suitable compounds and related extrusion techniques. There are plenty of examples of industrial cable installations where the use of ZH materials is now required to prevent damage to personnel or destruction of equipments. Metro (underground trains), public premises, oil platforms, are just a few cases where ZH cable are increasingly required. With the increment of energy requirements in hospitals, big closed public halls or block offices more high voltage cable are part of premises where requirements of ZH cables apply. It is possible to produce HV distribution cables (up to 18/30 kV) complying with the requirement of ZH cables and similar in design and handling to the conventional distribution cables. In order to evaluate their performance, one high voltage ZH cable for distribution purpose has been made and tested. The author presents the cable design and test results.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An instrument for the measurement of the quality of electricity
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The author outlines a development project for a low-priced instrument for the measurement of the quality of electricity. The background for this development is the growing interest in the concept of supply quality and the difficulties in the specification and documenting of the physical quantities which defines the quality. The developed instrument, a microprocessor based, 8 channels voltage and load analyser, its principles and features are described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Cables and Overhead Lines
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED

articleTitle: General approach of harmonic problems in industrial networks
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: Electronic power and control technology proliferates through industry, increasing both the number of disturbing loads (e.g. variable speed drives) and the number of sensitive loads (e.g. control devices, PCs, ripple control equipment, capacitors). Disturbance (i.e. deformation of the balanced and purely sinusoidal supply voltage) does not necessarily imply malfunctioning of equipment or processes. Such interference occurs only when the actual disturbance level is not compatible with the sensitive loads connected to the supply system. Compatibility problems may occur in totally new installations as well as in existing plants. The approach proposed in this paper takes into account the various aspects of the compatibility problem at hand, and the specific competence of the various parties involved in order to obtain an adequate solution.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Practical experience of 23 kV cable upgrading operation in Shanghai
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: In 1987, a paper entitled 'Reformation of the 23 kV cable network in Shanghai' was accepted by CIRED. As described, the upgrade project of 23 kV cable network in Shanghai has been executed continuously as planned. Along with the reformation of the distribution network, however, the up-graded cable circuits and it's total length varies, but up to now there are 26 circuits of 64.4 km in total length still in operation. Although these cables were made in the early period of this century and had been operated approximately 40 years before up-grade, they still keep a satisfied operation record with lower fault rate after up-grade. The author shows fault statistics and analysis of the cables.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Stresses of switching overvoltages in MW distribution networks with a high rate of cables and their influences on the selection of surge arresters
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: Environmental influences and the requirements imposed by the licensing authorities are making it necessary to install medium voltage distribution systems with more and more cables, even in sparsely populated areas. In terms of practical operation of the distribution systems, this poses the questions as to which overvoltages can occur in these systems and how to protect the equipment of the distribution system against such overvoltages. Here, the following calculations are performed with a view to answering these questions: switching on cables and overhead lines and of complete networks; disconnection of cables with restriking; initiation of ground faults; and clearing of system faults by the corresponding circuit breakers. The resultant surge voltages are determined and related to the stresses allowed for the items of equipment involved.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: INDUSTRIAL SYSTEMS AND CONSUMER INSTALLATION - ENERGY SAVING POLICIES AND TECHNIQUES
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED

articleTitle: Monitoring of voltage quality on distribution networks by means of portable instruments
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: In the frame of activities carried out by ENEL to improve the knowledge of the quality of supply in distribution networks, particular emphasis has been given to the acquisition of data on the characteristics of the voltage. To avoid the difficulties that normally arise when field measurements are carried out using different equipment and/or data processing criteria, it was decided to develop a standard recording instrument suitable for a widespread use by field agents. The authors describe the main construction characteristics of the instrument, the data processing procedures which have been implemented and the results obtained in some surveys which have been carried out.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: XLPE insulated MV cables: 20 years of experience in a Swiss network
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The authors present an evaluation of over 20 years of MV cable operation in a distribution network. Failures were recorded on the XLPE insulated cables installed since 1973; all of them occurred on cables manufactured before 1976. These are cables with a semi-conducting taped screen. Statistics on these failures are presented. Examinations (for faults, water trees) and electrical tests (impulse and 50 Hz) were performed in the laboratory on many cables which had failed in service. The results are compared to those obtained on new 1975 cables. Water has been detected in most of the failed cables. A campaign of sheath watertightness testing was carried out on about 100 cable lines. This revealed various sheath defects and damages. Finally, measurements of transient phenomena were recorded on the most severely affected part of the network. Results emerging from a first analysis are discussed. The conclusion summarizes the life expectancy of XLPE insulated MV cable as well as the criteria used when cables have to be changed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Safety and the environment, safety for bird life on electric lines
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The authors discuss the problems of birds colliding with overhead power lines and electrocution of birds. The authors discuss the measures taken by the Donana National Park in southern Spain, to protect the Imperial Iberian Eagle from the dangers of overhead lines by redesign of poles.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Reduced costs for customers and for utility by demand side management when refurbishing the supply system
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: Akered is a residential area in the south-west of Goteborg comprising 244 row houses and 233 linked houses. A time-of-day tariff is available for domestic customers with a consumption exceeding 10 MWh/year. The fixed annual charge is 788 SEK, independent of the size of the main fuses. All charges include energy tax and VAT. The switching between high and low prices has, up to now, been managed by an old local ripple control system. A new ripple control system is under installation which also makes centrally controlled load management possible. The present report describes the Swedish utilities' way of thinking, their objectives, their planning, performed activities and their experiences made up to now.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: MV/LV substations designed to look good
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: In the towns and villages supplied with electrical energy by the Compagnie vaudoise d'electricite (CVE), where requirements are continually increasing, customers appear less and less willing to allocate ground for siting the MV/LV substations necessary for public distribution of electricity. At the same time-as in all the worlds' industrialized countries-an increasing opposition to the external signs of industry can be felt among the population. Here, the author describes how for some time, to counter these trends, CVE has been developing a line of compactly dimensioned MV/LV substations, designed to be embedded in earth banks and therefore be unobtrusive while remaining inexpensive.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A comparative study of transformer cooling performance with fire-resistant dielectric fluids
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: Since the banning of PCBs, fire resistant dielectric fluids are often used where an extra margin of fire safety is needed. These dielectric coolants are also referred to as 'high fire point' and 'less-flammable' fluids. The most common fire resistant fluids have inferior cooling performance compared to both PCB based fluids and conventional transformer oils. The objective of this study is to compare the cooling performance of the alternate dielectric coolants, using both a mathematical model and actual heat runs. Comparison of the heat run data and the mathematical thermal model data indicated the fire resistant fluids performed with lower thermal gradients than predicted by the mathematical model calculations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The advantage of implementing corrective capacitors mounted directly on the low voltage side of a high voltage power transformer
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The authors describe the advantages of implementing corrective capacitors mounted directly on the low voltage side of a high voltage power transformer. These capacitors have two functions, namely: avoiding ferroresonance at the low voltage side; and reducing the inrush currents of a transformer. The elimination of ferroresonance can be achieved by connecting a capacitor of 2 mu F to earth on the low voltage side of a power transformer. The reduced inrush currents are the result of the limited remanent magnetism in the transformer, due to a switch off with a capacitor mounted directly on the low voltage side. Reduction of the inrush current ensures proper functioning of the differential protection.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Time-of-day electricity pricing using optimal mix of generation system
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: A systemic pricing method for power systems has been developed to obtain the time-of-day price for generation plant operation assessment and the time-of-day tariffs for consumer bill. The method presented by the authors is an hourly time-of-day pricing system based on the optimal mix of generation system. By means of time-of-day pricing, power plants are encouraged to follow peak load and consumers are guided to shift their peak demand to off-peak time of system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: MEB primary substations and the environment
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The author describes how the commitment by Midlands Electricity plc to protecting the environment has resulted in an intensive programme of bund wall construction around our primary substation power transformers. These walls are designed to contain any oil leak and so avoid the pollution of any adjacent water course, canal or public drainage system. Midlands Electricity is also committed to eliminating any nuisance to their customers caused by noise from transformers. All noise complaints are thoroughly investigated and acoustic enclosures or screens, are provided where necessary.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Computerized management of distribution network with a cadastral integrator
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: Knowledge of arborescent structures of low voltage networks and the necessity of load management in the different principal and secondary links has always been among the essential elements in the mastering of the distribution network evolution. The development of two new integrated computer tools makes it easier to manage networks while assuring the coherence in the collection of information, the efficiency in sorting and updating and finally time saving during graphic consultation with the help of a cadastral integrator or the use of an automatic generator of topological diagrams. The new GICAD cadastral module, achieved under the 'Windows' environment, is an integrator of graphic objects and alphanumeric technical or administrative data. It includes generation and file management routines allowing the documentation of topographic representations and therefore responds to the requests of network managers. The graphic interface programs include decompression operation and cadastral data compression taken from other data bases in order to adapt the size of files. It is therefore possible to integrate the network elements that accompany the topological representation like cable paths and their laying conditions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Cable system monitor
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The cable system monitor (CSM) has been designed to provide grid system managers with real-time computation of the load carrying capacity of selected cable circuits on the system. The increased thermal ratings that can be derived from the use of the CSM defer capital expenditure, reduce generation restrictions or the need for running security plant, allow greater access to the system for construction and maintenance, and postpone the need for re-negotiating wayleave consents. The significant advantage with the new monitor is the ability to retrieve the archived loading history so that similar days can be compared.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: New end-user services based on an advanced tariff computer system
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: A Danish electricity company, NESA, is carrying on a market survey of services to its consumers.
