The services are based on a newly developed tariff computer, TACOM, which is used for billing NESA's 15000 consumers who are being billed according to seasonal time-of-day tariffs. The market survey is divided into two parts. One applies to the industrial sector and the other applies to domestic consumers. The paper describes both surveys in detail and gives examples of some of the services offered.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Renovation of a larger substation within existing spatial limitations without discounting operations
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: In an electric distribution system, there is a need for continual renovation of its substations. The reasons for this can be many; e.g. high maintenance costs, lack of spare parts, unsatisfactory operational safety or inadequate performance. In an account of the renovation of a larger substation presented by the authors, all of these factors were present as well as the need to change the high voltage level from 50 kV to 130 kV. They give an exposition of the new technology used in the project with attention to coordinated concepts for microprocessor based control, monitoring and protection.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Product quality assurance by quality system and product certification
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: By using two Dutch companies, Holec and KEMA, the authors argue that it manufacturers who test products themselves demonstrably comply with the ISO 9001 and EN 45001 standards and if their products comply with international standards, this should automatically result in certification institutes granting recognized product certificates.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Studies of perturbations: their causes and effects on MT networks
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The authors present a broad outline of the research project that Iberdrola (a Spanish electrical utility) in collaboration with the Department of Electrical Engineering of the Polytechnic University of Valencia (Spain) has unfolded since 1990. It is analysing in addition to the power supply quality of the Spanish network, the relation between possible causes and effects over the customers. Provided that the study will include transient disturbance below 10 ms, not usually considered in power quality statistical fieldwork, testing and selecting the adequate disturbance recorder is one of the important stages. Moreover, the supplied power quality and the end-use devices requirements must be compatible, so this paper shows partial results obtained by sampling different market sectors.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Assessment of line current harmonics emitted by high power AC/DC converters
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: For an improved assessment of line current harmonics emitted by high power AC/DC converter, their amplitudes and phase angles are presented in normalized diagrams. The results are valid for six-pulse uncontrolled diode and controlled thyristor bridges, respectively, taking into account the influence of a rippled DC current.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Experiences in installation and operation for a sub-station control and protection system
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The authors describe how Iberdrola, the largest of Spain's private electric power utilities has recently, in conjunction with the Electrotecnica Arteche Hermanos Company and the Basque Country University, completed the installation of an integrated control and protection system at its Castro la Plana transformer substation. The purpose of the present paper is to describe the most salient aspects of its commissioning, and the advantages achieved in the operation and maintenance of this new installation, with special reference to those aspects which have involved an improvement over installations that are based on conventional control and protection systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: SF/sub 6/ medium-voltage circuit-breaker switchgear reliability improvement through a new gas chamber system
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The author describes how the gas chamber system of SF/sub 6/-insulated medium-voltage switchgear of the series type is provided with features which improves the dependability of the gaseous insulation and considerably facilitates monitoring of the gas chambers during operation. All three poles are surrounded by a common enclosure, which means the enclosure is 'three-pole'. This design therefore allows system complements tailored to the requirements of medium voltage. In addition, metal partitions are fitted between the poles of the three-pole conductor system, which provide a three-pole enclosure with features approaching those of single-pole enclosures.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Integration of real time control systems for electric utilities with emphasis on distribution management systems
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: In response to the operational objectives of quality and economy of electricity supply and customer service, much importance is given by utilities on improved tools and methods for the real time control of their power systems. A distribution management system (DMS) is defined in terms of its functions and in relation with other systems that are used by modern utilities. Two scenarios for the integration of these functions with other utility systems are presented. Both seem feasible but will differ in the way they communicate process and engineering information. There are important implementation limitations, partially imposed by the historical design and evolution of AM/FM packages and DMS software from distinctly different environments and partly due to the status of computer technology and software. The challenge for utilities and vendors is to create a solid software platform that permits the gradual incorporation of DMS applications step by step as they develop. On this basis the utilities' computer systems will integrate naturally.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Information system development for strategic management of an electricity supply utility
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The authors describe the features of an information technology architecture established at Prospect Electricity for the delivery of strategic computing systems. The underlying philosophy is also discussed with a view to defining a specific electricity supply industry information technology architecture based on the experienced gained. The information technology architecture is based on three layers defining the technology, data and application. The layers combine to form a powerful but flexible structure in which to address organisation wide information technology requirements. The critical success factors for the implementation are highlighted to guide organisations considering a similar path.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new look at electrical supply quality and profitability
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The search for improved quality of supply, and profitability, requires a detailed knowledge of electrical system performance at the time of occurrence. Customer voltage profiles, and other system performance figures, such as total system loss and network profitability, are usually available, but at some future time. Without this intimate knowledge of system performance, corrective equipment, such as voltage control devices, load switching and capacitor banks cannot be used to maximum impact. A set of algorithms, which calculate customer voltage profiles, system loss and network profitability from readily available zone substation information are described. The author also describes the use of programmable logic controllers (PLC), within the zone substation of a distribution network to give improved customer supply voltage, assist in reducing system losses and increasing network profitability.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Disturbances generated by power rectifiers: existing solutions and future prospects
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: Single and three-phase thyristors and diodes bridges are the most widely-used type of power rectifiers at present. A poor power factor current harmonics and switching pulses are the main types of disturbances they generate. The authors briefly describe them and then detail their effects on distribution networks. They next detail existing and potential methods of satisfactorily connecting power converters to the network. These methods include, amongst other possibilities, the development of active filters, possibly combined with passive filters, and power factor correction bridges. Actions aimed at limiting disturbances introduced by this type of converter include promoting the use of these circuits and developing standards limiting the emission from LV equipment sold to the general public but also modifications to the networks (a larger number of primary substations, increased Psc (short-circuit power)) and the development of contracts concerning the quality of electricity between electricity utilities and customers.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: MV-capacitive electronic voltage detectors: conclusions from comprehensive type tests based on the new IEC-draft
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: In many MV substations, the safety of operation relies on the use of voltage detectors in order to verify that the circuits are effectively unenergized before to connect them to earth. Electronic capacitive voltage detectors have become more and more widespread. Up to now they were only covered by very different national standards mainly in France and Germany. This lead to the development of two strongly different detector types. Recently WG 7 of IEC committee 78 worked out a draft covering all capacitive voltage detectors above 1 kV. Here, the authors describe how they undertook a comparative study on a large variety of equipment of voltages from 6.6-15 kV and 36 kV. The IEC document was the basis of the test program.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Collection, transmission and treatment of requirements for control of the urban cable network of 22 kV
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The author deals with the control of an urban cable network of 22 kV. The power supply will be made more reliable and efficient as the control information is made more timely and accurate. The system provides the following features: reliable determination of the location of failure and its remote indication; fast delimination of the damaged section by remote control; reduction of the down time for consumers; increase in security for working staff; and improved economics of the cable system of 22 kV. The founding of the presumptions mentioned and of building the control system follows the universal validity of the algorithm-the removing of failure states in the urban cable network without the information and control system being built.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Remote control and diagnosis of the 36 kV substations in the Brussels area
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The variety of the systems installed in the substations, the shortage of available information, and the constantly increasing complexity of the network led to the setting up of a work team with the mission of defining an efficient tool for the Brussels Regional Transmission Centre. Two objectives were laid down: to update the dispatching centre in Schaerbeek, and to equip the substations with systems that would facilitate control and maintenance. The modernization of the dispatching centre in Schaerbeek was completed in 1989. It was decided to equip the substations with a numerical control system, completed with an additional automatic device for network restoration. The authors discuss the operation of the network and describe the substation control system, its operation and its advantages.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Aspects on an integrated distribution management system
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: An integrated distribution management system (DMS) can provide the utilities with the functionality and upgrade flexibility that will be required to meet the emerging challenges imposed by the free energy markets. The benefits from integrating the corporate information systems on a common platform is outlined and discussed. Then the realization of an integrated DMS environment is addressed, and it is shown how the open system architecture of the SPIDER DMS facilitates the vertical and horizontal integration of the different corporate information systems. Finally, the data engineering tools supporting the data management coordination on this integrated environment are described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Computer model to evaluate the reliability of substations. Application to a specific case
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The authors deal with the description of a computer model designed to study the reliability of substations. This model has been used in the planning of the electrical supply to the 1992 Universal Exhibition in Seville in order to discover exactly which model of all of those studied would offer the sufficient degree of reliability required by the Exhibition authorities. The authors apply the model to three variants of a single bar substation: with breakers; with disconnectors; and with remote control disconnectors. Each corresponding degree of reliability is assessed by extracting ratios of reliability/investment which show the advantages of each possibility. In conclusion they can see the limits of maximum power and energy consumption justifying each case.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Cogeneration power plants by gas turbines in industrial installations: connection to the internal electrical system, interface with external grid, protection schemes
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: Cogeneration power plants, using gas turbines operating in combined cycle, are today spreading in industries, for the production of electrical energy and steam. This trend is due to several reasons, i.e. more efficient use of fuel, the availability of waste fuels as a consequence of production processes, the requirements of a quite reliable source of electrical energy for vital loads and the opportunity of selling excess energy to external Board at profitable prices. The selection of the most convenient connection point of the power plant to the electrical distribution network of the industrial installation requires a detailed analysis of the existing power schemes, in order to ensure maximum reliability and availability to critical loads, flexibility with respect to load management and to keep fault currents within the sizing of existing apparatus. Attention should be paid to the problem of interface with the external grid: the prescriptions of the Electrical Authority Board shall be complied with as well as national or international recommendations or standards, and in the meantime it is mandatory to satisfy all the requirements of the production process. The authors illustrate several problems to be faced in the design of cogeneration power plants inside different industrial installations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Development of subduct installation method inside the duct with the power cable
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: For the future information-oriented society, the demand for high-volume information transfer using optical fiber cable is increasing. However, installation of a new protective conduit exclusively for optical fiber cable in an urban area presents many problems. Tokyo Electric Power Company and Hitachi Cable have developed a practical technique to lay optical fiber cable in a conduit in which a power cable has been already installed. The authors describe this system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Numerical tools for auto-expansion in SF/sub 6/ circuit-breakers
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The authors present the results of a project whose objective was the development of a numerical method for the design and optimisation of circuit breakers. The research concentrated on modelling the arc-gas interactions in a SF/sub 6/ auto-expansion circuit breaker. In the chosen modelling, the arc core and the surrounding gas are considered as a continuous medium governed by a single set of equations. The adopted numerical method is a 'finite volume' one. It is adapted to take into account compressibility and real gas properties, Joule losses in the arc, radiative exchanges and energy transport by convection and conduction.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Development of common remote-control meter reading system
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: Along with the development of advanced urban functions in the information-oriented society, the society's high dependency on electric power has increased. Under the circumstances, Kansai Electric Power Co., Inc. has been positively tackling the technical development for materializing a totally automated power distribution system, which aims at high standardization and higher reliability of electric power facilities. As part of the technical development, they have developed a system that enables not only electric power but gas and other enterprises cooperatively to perform remote control meter reading and provide information and load control for customers. In this paper, the authors introduce an outline of the system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Meter reading by DREMS (dual-mode residential energy monitoring system)
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: Cairo Electricity Distribution Company (CEDC) has over 3.5 million subscribers consuming monthly over 1200 Megawatt hours of electric energy. About 30% of their meters are inaccessible in a typical month due to closed apartments. Most of the meters are located inside the apartments. Over a thousand meter readers and a thousand clerks are involved in collecting, listing and processing monthly consumption and status of data in 24 dispatch stations. Automation was previously limited to a central mainframe for issuing bills. The authors present the outline of the new DREMS system, its features and benefits. In addition, the critical issues of selecting hardware and software components are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Research of critical electric fields in accessories for power cables
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: In studies, design or malfunction examination involving power cables accessories, it is important to locate the areas where the electric field can reach critical values and to know its components. The authors explain how an electric field computation software allows this kind of problem to be solved. This highly interactive software is based on a computation method well suited for problem solutions where the geometries are lengthy as is often the case for cable accessories. The computation of a time-harmonic analysis allows the resistivity of materials to be taken into account. Two practical examples show the application of this investigation method and high voltage accessories.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Restructuring of the high-voltage system in a city-effects on the 10 kV system configuration and system operation
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: Various installations in a 60/10 kV city network have grown old as the system has expanded over the years; this leads to high maintenance and inspection costs. There is so far no other way of assuring the reliability and availability of supplies. Despite substantial support in the form of energy-saving measures implemented by the supply utility (and the resulting general slowing down of growth), there will be no alternative but to renew these installations. Further factors such as the closing down of a power plant (for reasons of environmental protection) necessitate additional expansion measures. The authors analyse the existing supply situation and report on restructuring in the 10 kV network and on the resultant possibilities offered by an expansion variant with 110/10 kV. The authors also describe how isolated installation renewal, together with coordinated practical planning of the medium and high-voltage levels can be the first step in building up a modern supply system for the future.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Computer controlled meter test systems for domestic & industrial meters
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The authors outline their approach to the design and manufacture of meter test systems. The Company has the capability to design and manufacture the hardware; and write the software for all aspects of meter test systems. The approach is flexible in terms of the users entry level and system components required. The authors comment in detail on some of the problems associated with the design and implementation of new phantom load systems (PLS) as this is the area of greatest change at the moment. Detailed specifications are given for power generation to clarify the problem. The techniques used for computer control of the PLS and the generation of a multiphase sinusoidal system are described. The approach to efficient power generation is also covered. Comments are made on the data collection and archiving.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Electronic energy meters-principles, performances and tests
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The different principles used by the manufacturers of electronic watt-hour meters for LV consumers are presented. The digital and the analog techniques are distinguished with their specific characteristics. The authors also give, in a synthetic manner the results of evaluation tests performed by Laborelec on commercially available domestic watthour meters from different manufacturers.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: ADER-a software to aid decision makers for distribution network maintenance and renewal
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: Maintenance and replacement operations for power system equipment aim to improve the reliability and safety. Electricite de France is developing a decision aid interactive system to help the user of an electric network make optimal decisions regarding the maintenance. The authors describe the ADER software program which comprises: a network interactive graphic database management system; an expert system to determine the potential weak-points of a network and their relative seriousness; an analysis of the incidents which occurred during the preceding years; and a maintenance or replacement decision aid based on the above dual analysis, taking into account a number of nationwide or unitwide parameters. This system requires only a light hardware configuration of the compatible PC microcomputer type and can consequently be set up within the most decentralised operation teams.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Modernisation of a regional energy distribution network
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The political changes in the east of Germany have created completely new requirements for the technical and economic boundary conditions of the supply of electrical energy. The authors describe the resulting demands with regard to the configuration of distribution networks and their technical realisation, taking the example of a large regional power utility, Mitteldeutsche Energieversorgung Aktiengesellschaft MEAG. The new statutory stipulations and market demands mean not only economic efficiency and ecological compatibility but also a high supply quality, characterised by a sufficient in-time presentation of energy to all customers, high-quality voltage and short resupply times. The authors describe the measures needed to achieve the sub-goals mentioned on the basis of future network planning and operational management strategies, the interaction of concepts and their implementation to set up a modern energy supply system. They highlight the problems as well as the possibilities produced by the extraordinary situation of a relatively short-term, comprehensive restructuring of total networks of such a size.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Convergences and divergences in distribution investment between industrialised and developing countries
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The economic and political contexts of a country have a considerable effect on the development of its electrical sector and on that of its distribution network in particular. These parameters are reviewed and analysed. The basic data for this analysis is derived from the experience acquired by the authors through studies related to the development of distribution networks in Europe, particularly in Belgium, and in numerous countries in Africa and Latin America. The parameters essential for selecting distribution network investments have been structured as follows: the equipment existing in the network and the new equipment to be selected for its development; the cost of distribution and the structure of such costs; the quality of service expected by consumers and that really ensured by the electricity company; electrical power demand characteristics and its evolution; and environmental constraints.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Clink, a cost effective, high performance data collection, protection and control system for LV industrial switchboards
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: Not so long ago, a great deal of auxiliary wiring was incorporated in the controlling and signalling of low voltage motor control switchgear. Nowadays more and more electronic systems are emerging which carry out these functions by communicating via a single bus. Some systems also offer fairly sophisticated protection functions, for instance improved thermal protection of motor loads. Clink is just such a system, developed by Holec Systemen en Componenten B.V. The authors give a brief description of how Clink works, and then examine some of the design aspects in greater detail. The first of these is communication, the basic lifeline in this kind of system. They take a look at system reliability in general and its electromagnetic compatibility. Finally, an explanation is given of special, construction measures taken in order to fulfil the requirements placed by aspects mentioned above.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Ecological effects of changes in the design of distribution cables
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The author discusses the importance of material re-use in distribution cables. Existing cable waste is discussed as are the problems of PVC and other polymers removal. The principles of metal reclamation and the recycling methods. The design of new cables to ensure improved utilisation of recoverable materials is discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A modern distribution management system
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The authors present an open, modular, expandable network automation system which meets the requirements for management of distribution networks-a distribution management system (DMS). The distributed system architecture based on servers and workstations is explained, and the standards used (e.g. operating system, communication protocols, graphical user interface) are noted. The requirements which must be met by the SCADA functions for control and monitoring of a distribution network and typical distribution management functions are described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Expert system for user connection analyses
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The expert system (ES) described has been conceived to manage the technical aspects of the connection of user installations to the public supply networks, including the electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) problems. An expert system offers the most effective solution to the problem, due to its ability to combine analytic and heuristic rules and to the possibility of expanding and changing the rules to comply with new requirements, with a minimal effort. In using the ES, the connection cases are dealt with by applying uniform and well defined criteria, thus minimizing the effect of subjective interpretations. The ES has been conceived to run on a graphic workstation, hosting also the information system for distribution networks developed by ENEL, so that the operator can readily access the database describing the network and make use of the calculation programs forming part of the information system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: DISTURBANCES AND PROTECTION IN SUPPLY SYSTEMS
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED

articleTitle: Optimizing the power system impacts of demand-side management
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: With an increasing emphasis on demand-side management (DSM) as an alternative to more traditional power system expansion methods, utility planners are required to conduct more comprehensive analyses in order to achieve a satisfactory integration of supply-side and demand-side technologies. DSM impacts are typically manifested in varying degrees at each level of the power system. Thus, the complexity of optimizing an electrical power system is increased under the DSM option. The authors discuss the fundamental issues of DSM impacts, particularly with respect to the transmission and distribution portions of the power system. The nature of the characteristic differences of the customer classes, the importance of DSM market penetration, and the utilization of system reconfiguration are emphasized with regard to achieving maximum system benefits.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A design study on voltage controlled rectifier sub-stations for a rapid transit railway
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The authors describe a particular DC distribution problem experienced on London Underground's Central Line renewal project consisting of excessive volt-drop in a particular tunnel section. Three systems studies have been described on DC distribution assessment, AC distribution assessment and EMC relating to signalling compatibility, for the proposed use of voltage controlled rectifiers (VCRs). It has been found that VCRs can provide a solution to the problem of unacceptable voltage drop. It has also been found that VCRs need a stiff AC distribution system for proper operation. The study has shown that power factor is reduced and that harmonic distortion increases with the use of VCRs. An EMC problem of operating VCRs with existing power frequency signalling equipment has been identified and quantified. An engineering systems solution has been proposed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On site MV-cable testing with AC-voltages
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: For testing MV-cables on site, there are quite different approaches in use. In the past mainly DC-testing was used, but for several years, different designs for test voltage sources have appeared. The cable manufacturers and research institutes no longer recommend DC-testing for PE/XLPE cables with aged dielectric. The authors discuss AC testing and in particular the resonant test set. The aims of the testing, test extensions, and practical experience are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Planning of medium voltage distribution networks by dynamic models
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The authors describe a dynamic model designed to investigate network development over a time span of twenty years, which has been found to be particularly effective for improved long-term planning (strategic planning). In particular the algorithm gives the approximate optimum network configurations at five year intervals and these results are then available for short-medium term planning (operative planning). The latter activity has also formed the subject of a dedicated program which allows optimum location of the HV/MV substations and the associated best configuration of MV networks, whilst satisfying all the technical constraints. Besides describing this algorithm, the authors also deal with the problem of load forecasting and emphasize the increasingly important role assumed by active strategic monitoring of demand, promoted by the utility, in rationalization of the investment process.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Overvoltages on the low voltage distribution networks. Origins and characteristics. Consequences upon the construction of Electricite de France networks
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: Overvoltages on the LV distribution networks can be classified into two types, temporary and transient. The most important transient overvoltages mainly originate in a lightning stroke occurring either on the MV network side and which propagate throughout the LV network via the MV/LV substation or near to an LV network. Electricite de France currently limits the temporary overvoltages on LV conductors to 1500 Vrms according to the regulations in effect. With regard to transient overvoltages, studies and experiments carried out enabled proving that they are generally below 8 kV and might, given certain configurations, be as high as 14 kV excepting any direct lightning stroke.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Operation and Control in Power Supply Systems
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED

articleTitle: Improving the mechanical reliability of medium-voltage overhead lines: controlled extension devices, flexible insulators and anti-spinning masses
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The authors present the two types of flexible insulators developed by several manufacturers, as well as the results of their experimentation in progress. They also show the gain in admissible overload provided by combined use of flexible insulators and controlled extension devices. Finally, the approach that made it possible to define criteria for installation on the lines already in place and, in certain cases, on new lines (geographical area, number, associated mechanical overload, etc.) of the anti-spinning masses is discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A method for optimal sizing of reactive power compensation capacitors for industrial power systems
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The author presents a new method for optimal sizing of fixed or automatically switched reactive power compensation capacitors for industrial power systems. The capacitor locations considered are substations, motor control centres and motor locations. In the method the size of capacitors is optimized with respect to the costs of power losses, energy losses and investments.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The ENEL distribution automation system
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The authors describe the most important features of a new distribution automation system, conceived by ENEL in order to provide an overall solution to the two most important aspects concerning the automation of on-line activities related to electricity distribution: remote control of distribution power networks; and customer services automation and control. The system allows the remote control of any component of the ENEL distribution network, starting from the HV/MV substations to metering apparatus installed at LV customer premises and also opens the door towards the development of applications concerning home and building automation systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Benefits of gapped MOV arrester to improve system reliability and extend equipment life
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: It is not often the nature permits one benefit without compromising another. The authors detail however, in the case of a new series gapped metal oxide varistor (MOV) for system overvoltage protection, a dramatically lower protective level is achieved while providing an increased temporary overvoltage (TOV) capability. These benefits may seem paradoxical, but are a result of the unique interaction of a resistance-graded gap and the MOV disk stack.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: DESIGN AND PLANNING OF PUBLIC SUPPLY SYSTEMS
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED

articleTitle: MV transportable, remote controlled unit for HV/MV sub-stations
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: In the last few years there has been growing interest in mobile HV/MV substations. This paper examines the MV unit of these substations which have recently been the object of important development. The use of the new compact SF/sub 6/ GIS means the system can be installed in standard containers making transport and set up both fast and easy. Moreover the use of microprocessor-based control and protection devices interfaced with a computer makes local and remote control of whole system extremely simple.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Some recent developments in ESB IN: (A) environmental line design (B) design/specification of ABC line components
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The first part of this two part paper is concerned with environmental 38 kV line design in Ireland. It describes the considerations and options leading to the particular design chosen (single steel poles with polymeric composite insulators) and reviews the construction experience gained so far. The second part considers three developments in low voltage ABC (aerial bundled conductor) line components, waterproof insulation piercing connectors, pole fuse combination units and wear testing of suspension clamps. The background leading to these developments is described and particular attention is given to their specification/testing which has not, as yet, been agreed internationally.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Qualification tests performed on composite insulators for 132-150 kV overhead lines
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: Composite insulators may be prone in service to damage of the external housing (tracking, split, erosion, chalking) and of the core (mechanical failure). An IEC Standard was issued that ENEL applied, with some adaptation and implementation, in performing the insulator qualification. As for a tracking and erosion test, two alternative procedures are given by the IEC Standard to reproduce the service stresses in severe ambients. To cover the risk of fractures in service due to fatigue and stress corrosion of the insulator core, ENEL studied and defined a mechanical-chemical long term test. The authors describe the results of the above mentioned tests obtained on a few types of composite insulators of the latest production. For the two insulator types that have now passed all the planned tests, a pilot service experience is going to start on 132-150 kV line sections chosen all over Italy.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A practical approach to the use, siting and setting-up of distribution equipment and its protection
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to demonstrate that certain specialist technical subjects, in this case distribution protection, can be successfully taught to modestly qualified staff who often have only a limited understanding of networks and protection. The appropriate technical knowledge required to complement their practical know-how is presented in a comprehensive but straight forward manner. The subjects taught include fault level calculations using symmetrical components. The need for, use and siting of pole mounted switchgear and the characteristics of source switchgear. Also included are the principles needed to enable all the associated protection to be graded safety and correctly.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: New method of fault location in MV systems
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The authors present a new, low-cost fault location process for the configuration of protection equipment in MV power systems. On the basis of theoretical fundamentals, the authors first present simulation results, then go on to describe their implementation in a substation control system. Evidence is presented to show that this process is fundamentally capable of functioning effectively: this evidence takes the form of results from short-circuit experiments performed on single-pole faults in a 10 kV system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Testing a new real time tariff for the residential clientele
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: Demand by EDF customers has evolved considerably: as a result of the development of electric heating, power requirements are closely linked to the season and peaks occur during cold weather. These are therefore concentrated over a small number of winter days not known in advance. In order to adapt to this situation, the EDF is considering real time tariff options. Thus, in the residential sector, an option based on the splitting up of the year in real time is planned. This new option of the blue tariff, intended for customers who need less than 36 kVA, is called 'BLUE, WHITE, RED'; it includes 3 kinds of random days. Each day is divided into 2 fixed periods. This option is particularly interesting for customers who agree to reduce their electricity consumption in high-price periods. This new tariff option is currently being tested in 7 EDF GDF SERVICES centres and concerns around 800 customers.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Demonstration of the feasibility of the use of amorphous magnetic material as transformer core material
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: No load losses in distribution transformer cores are estimated to consume at least 3% of all energy generated in Europe. Energy efficient distribution transformer cores are made from high quality grain oriented silicon iron laminations having losses of around 0.8 W/kg at 1.5 T. Amorphous magnetic material has losses of around 30% that of the best quality silicon iron. The material is difficult to use because it is thin and its magnetic properties are very stress sensitive. This paper outlines work being carried out as part of a THERMIE project to demonstrate the energy saving potential of amorphous magnetic materials. Transformers ranging from 25 kVA to 315 kVA have been designed with wound toroidal cores. The losses are expected to be 25-30% of equivalent transformers with conventional cores. An estimate of the benefit of widespread replication is made.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: AEPD: an artificial intelligence based tool for underground residential distribution design
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The design of an underground residential distribution (URD) system for new residential development is an everyday task to electric utility engineers. Puget Sound Power & Light Co. (PSPL) and the University of Washington (UW) have jointly developed a tool for the computerized (automated) design of residential underground electric supply systems, called Automated Electrical Plat Design (AEPD). The computerized tool speeds up the design process and allows an URD system to be designed more economically and to operate closer to its limits. The concept and development of this tool is discussed by the authors. The AEPD concept shows synergy that can be gained by integrating a geographic information system and artificial intelligence in the area of electric distribution planning and design. The concepts presented are generic and can be applied to a host of problems in the distribution planning and design area with spatial components.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Field experience on improving corrosion performance of OH lines crossarms and concrete poles
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: Tamil Nadu Electricity Board (TNEB) supplies power to about 9 million consumers through a vast distribution system consisting of over 90000 distribution transformers, 0.09 million km HV lines and 0.4 million km LV lines. Most of the distribution lines are overhead lines with aluminium-conductor-steel-reinforced (ACSR). The pole supports of these lines are of either reinforced cement concrete (RCC) or prestressed cement concrete (PSC). The crossarms are of mild steel coated with anti-corrosive paint. Breakdowns of lines are caused by conductor snapping, crossarm failure and deterioration of pole. They lead to interruptions in power supply and heavy expenditure on rectification, besides wastage of manpower as well as materials for the utility and loss of production for the consumers. TNEB took up research projects to analyse such failures, arrive at probable causes, make remedial suggestions and monitor their effectiveness to decide on the suitability. The studies have helped identification of the remedial measures that suit the TNEB for mitigating supply interruptions caused by line breakdowns on account of the premature failure of conductors, crossarms and poles.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Optimisation of the selection and use of protections in numerical controlled substations. Application in Belgium
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: Substation secondary equipment is today exposed to important technical innovations. Since the advent of the microprocessor in numerical protection and control, this technology has become common place in modern substations. Selecting protection equipment for numerical controlled substations leads one straight to the numerical relays. This report illustrates the potential offered by digital protection in a numerical controlled substation. An illustration of the growing optimisation of protection techniques is given by the 36 kV substation of Langerbrugge. This important supply station in the Belgian power distribution system is supplied by three 110 MVA transformers 150/36 kV, two turbo-generators of 20 MVA and 40 MVA, and a turbo-jet generator of 18 MW, and consists of a double busbar system with a bus coupler and 24 feeders. More precisely, this 36 kV substation will be equipped with digital feeder protection based on distance or overcurrent algorithms and digital busbar protection.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: New method for assessing the disturbance level of a distribution system
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: Few electric utilities go beyond current IEC and ANSI requirements regarding the thresholds of harmonic distortion, voltage unbalance, overvoltages and voltage dips on their distribution lines on a full-time basis. Technical document IEC 1000-2-1 stipulates that those threshold values should be respected at least 95% of the time, while the draft of revised ANSI standard 519 states that specified values may be exceeded for short intervals. Thus, during certain periods of time no limits are specified; hence the need for some means of characterizing disturbances and defining thresholds that are better adapted to modern power systems. The authors therefore propose a new approach based on the thermal energy accumulated by the equipment affected by power system disturbances. In addition to a redefinition of the steady-state value, an energy-related index is given for better identifying the nature of fluctuating system disturbances.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: 16 years of fault statistics in the Dutch LV, MV and HV distribution networks; results and progress
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: Nonavailability of distribution networks due to fault is strongly related to the quality of electricity supply to consumers. The author provides an overview of the period 1976 up to and including 1991. Regarding LV and MV the survey relates to about two thirds of the total number of consumers in the Netherlands, while the HV survey applies to the whole of the country. The survey method has developed over the years from forms being filled out on the spot all the way to automated performance by way of a computer program called NESTOR.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The effect of new tariffs on electric domestic space heating
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The authors demonstrate that an electric heating system using a mix of storage and direct acting heaters can operate with complex tariffs to provide improved thermal comfort at reduced cost to the user and the generation and distribution companies. The development of the novel control method for the mixed mode system was enabled by the development of detailed computer simulations of the household environment using a modular simulation language. The validated simulation model, coupled with an evaluation of the system in two test houses, has demonstrated that the heating system can respond to customers' heating requirements. Furthermore, the system can be set up without accurate knowledge of the thermal performance of the building.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Analysis, experience and planning of electrical distribution networks during storms, rain, snow, wind, etc., but especially floods
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The authors describe the experience gained during the 1980s on the behaviour of electrical distribution networks during great storms and specially during the autumn floods caused by the penetration of unusually cold air-currents at the higher levels of the troposphere, causing torrential rain and floods which are the main factors for the deficient quality of electrical supply, thus causing serious damages to companies and clients. The authors analyse the causes of supply-interruptions as well as supply-quality according to the needs of the clientele; study the areas, affected plants, undistributed energy (UE), damage-evaluation, etc.; and state the activity of operational personnel, work-organisation and accident-prevention. The authors propose solutions to improve the quality and reliability of installations, pre-project studies for siting transformation centres and substations, and networks, and integrated planning for future distribution networks.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Service interruptions: the customers' views
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: Conventional wisdom holds that, after safety, the minimum threshold to favorable customer opinion in the electric utility industry is satisfactory service dependability. In other words, if service dependability (or 'reliability') is poor, everything else a utility does will be viewed as poor by customers. The utility that intends to remain successful should stay abreast of its customers' perceptions. To this end, Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PG&E) periodically surveys its customers to better understand their attitudes toward service dependability and other customer service issues. A 1990 study focused on the perception of residential and commercial customers of their electric service dependability. The goal was to improve their understanding of customers' perceptions of service dependability. They also hoped this knowledge would help pinpoint locations or customer segments where service dependability improvements would have the most beneficial effect on customers' perception at the lowest cost. The results were used to determine the relationship between customers' overall satisfaction with PG&E and several measures of service dependability.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Load modelling method at distribution level. Activity-hourly-groups approximation (GHAC)
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The GHAC method for load modelling at distribution level has been developed to obtain, separately, the curves of active and reactive demanded power on MV/LV and HV/MV substations. The authors have tested its applicability to obtain models able to add sorts of loads and customer, using data coming from utilities. Among the outer variables considered are human behaviour and climatic variations. The use of the activity hourly groups have allowed reproduction of the evolution of the load without the necessity of individual device modelling. The modelling method is absolutely applicable to a wide range of geographic and climatic situations and it has been probed with real data recorded during three years at MV/LV and HV/MV substations in Iberdrola, a Spanish public utility.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Development of an end-use monitoring system
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: There is a trend for electricity supply industry utilities to focus on the demand side to solve issues of supply and demand. This approach has been become known as demand side management (DSM). Here, the authors outline how end-use monitoring is an important part of gathering field data for a DSM program. The object in establishing an end-use survey is to collect energy use data of sufficient detail to allow a DSM program to be formulated with confidence and its impact to be successfully evaluated. The level and nature of end-use monitoring is determined by the class of consumer ie. domestic, commercial or industrial.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Architecture of HV/MV substation protection and control equipment using digital technology application to the MV substation EDF 'la Cazerie' (EGS Rouen)
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: In order to improve the quality of service to its customers, Electricite de France has decided to make important changes in the coming years, which will affect the HV/MV substation protection-control systems evolution. Consequently, the increase in the number of MV networks placed underground, and evolution in the neutral earthing condition will lead to major changes in the protection plan. The authors describe how the implementation of this plan, together with the necessary renewal of equipment, particularly MV cubicles, makes it necessary to rethink HV/MV substation protection-control taking account of the availability of digital technology.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Reliability of conception and operation for SF/sub 6/-insulated MV equipment
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: Among the different aspects of electrical switchgear, dependability is certainly the characteristic for which the users have the highest expectations of improvement. The aim of this contribution is, after a short reminder on dependability, to show how a manufacturer can fulfil this need of improvement. The differences between air insulated and SF/sub 6/ insulated metal-enclosed switchgear are then evaluated to show how the guidelines of dependability influence the development process: ISO series 9001, calculations, qualification tests, ergonomics, diagnostics, etc.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: How to answer sensitive customers expectations (power supply quality)
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: Quality has become the hallmark of the economy and the prerequisite for good customer/supplier relations. In an ever-more demanding context, EDF has to live with its times and has to make power supply quality its prime objective. In addition to the standard of service to be rendered to the clientele, this general desire necessitates improvement of the quality of supply. Vis-a-vis its customers, this willingness formalises its commitment which comprises indemnification should it fail in its duty. In this respect, two broad complementary lines of action are in progress: the 'EMERALD' contract, with the optional 'System Plus' contract; and the service 'Quality' Plus and the 'High Quality' Zones in which responses to customer's problems are provided in collaboration with the installers and the local communities, which enables each actor to play its role in the quest for customer service.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Advanced metalclad switchgear equipment
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The authors explain how continuously increasing demands are imposed on medium voltage switchgear. Both SF/sub 6/ and modern air insulated switchgear meet these demands. A new development in the category of air-insulated switchgear is introduced here, which exhibit interesting features in the case of a cubicle as well as for the newly developed vacuum circuit breaker. A description of an integrated power system control and protection system with promising characteristics shows that a substation can be described as completed only when it includes a suitable control and monitoring system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Network structure in sub-transmission systems. Features and practices in different countries
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The authors deal with network architecture in general and the role of sub-transmission in particular. They describe the results of a study carried out by a combined CIRED/CIGRE Working Group. It gives condensed information on the practice in about 14 different countries and examples of network structures in the United Kingdom, Belgium, Italy and the Netherlands. The density and size of substations and the number of transformers are examined. Relevant planning aspects regarding sub-transmission network structures are studied. Some aspects of the planning and design process are described. Quality of service and reliability are treated. An important parameter determining the reliability is the available reserve capacity in the network.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Experience with operational management systems for power distribution networks, with special emphasis on remote control and the use of 'artificial intelligences'
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The use of 'artificial intelligences' in network management systems relieves the burden on the network manager, particularly in stress situations. With the introduction of digital station instrumentation and control technology, the network manager, when confronted with a fault, can now call up all the malfunction parameters available in the station. With the aid of 'artificial intelligences', these data, in conjunction with the messages being received by the network management system and the network topology image stored in the computer's memory, can be used to locate the fault concerned. The authors summarize the experience gained with these network management systems, indicating the reasons which led to expansion of what was originally an annunciation system to incorporate a remote control option, and describing the intended enhancements featuring 'artificial intelligences'. The computer-aided network management systems have proved their worth. Initial experience with remote control shows that the anticipated advantages have been obtained.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Overhead power lines designed to contain failure
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: Age related problems in line components such as rot in wood poles, corrosion of conductors, crossarms, stays, fittings and steel towers need to be considered when measuring system reliability to withstand the severe hurricanes and blizzards periodically encountered in the UK. The authors describe such an occurrence in December 1990 within the East Midlands region, where weather conditions of unprecedented severity caused severe damage to the region's LV-132 kV overhead line network. There will always be problems with inclement weather, especially for a power network. The authors review techniques such as failure containment, improved standards and the advent of optical fibres. Weather conditions such as those described are impossible to cater for in line design but by careful selection of failure containment measures, the disastrous effect on system security can be considerably reduced.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An energy efficient demonstration home for Canberra, Australia
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Electricity Distribution, 1993. CIRED
abstract: The development, construction and operation of an energy efficient home is described. The home is designed to be efficient not only in its direct, local use of electrical energy but also efficient in local water use and sewerage generation, reducing the energy used for water supply and wastewater treatment. Canberra is unusual in that a single statutory authority is responsible for all three services.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
